stem.en: Why does the nuclear shell model predict that certain heavier superheavy nuclei could be more stable than their lighter neighbours, rather than expecting stability to decline smoothly with mass?
stem.et: Miks ennustab tuuma kihimudel, et teatud raskemad ülirasked tuumad võiksid olla stabiilsemad kui nende kergemad naabrid, mitte oodata stabiilsuse sujuvat langust massiga?

label.en: Because closed proton and neutron shells produce local peaks of extra stability regardless of overall mass, the same effect behind ordinary magic-number nuclei.
label.et: Sest kinnised prooton- ja neutronikihid tekitavad kohalikke lisastabiilsuse tippe olenemata kogumassist, sama efekt, mis on tavaliste maagilise arvuga tuumade taga.

label.en: It doesn't -- stability declines smoothly and monotonically with atomic number, with no possibility of any local exception.
label.et: Ei ennusta -- stabiilsus langeb sujuvalt ja monotoonselt aatomnumbriga, ilma võimaluseta mistahes kohalikuks erandiks.

label.en: Because the island of stability has already been reached and confirmed by superheavy elements synthesized so far, which are fully stable.
label.et: Sest stabiilsuse saar on juba saavutatud ja kinnitatud seni sünteesitud üliraskete elementide poolt, mis on täiesti stabiilsed.

label.en: Because superheavy elements are produced in large, bulk quantities, allowing their stability to be measured the same way ordinary elements are.
label.et: Sest üliraskeid elemente toodetakse suurtes, hulgikogustes, mis lubab nende stabiilsust mõõta samamoodi nagu tavaliste elementide oma.
